system.summary: The cipher of targets/ceva1632: two-digit codes for letters (homophones) and syllables, the ten pairs 2x as nulls, a lone 6 as word space, and three-digit codes for words and names.
system.doubled_letters: not written: the cipher writes no double letters
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the code groups of the key in key-and-key-free-read/key.tsv: 62 pair codes with a value (61 of the published key, plus pair 33), the 10 null pairs 2x, 46 three-digit codes with a value on the pages and the word space 6. nomenclator.entries counts the three-digit codes with a value on the pages: 28 ledger values of the first pass less 129, which the pages leave open, and 19 values that the ledger read but did not adopt, shown as conjectures. One code stands for u and v; homophones counts it as a vowel (u_v).

prior_solution.where: Decipherment leaves of the time in R5626 (f. 155r), R5637 (f. 212v) and R5646 (f. 269r); Brice Dudout's notes add R5655 (f. 324). Leman (1920) used the Barberini minutes of the cipher despatches to Ceva; not checked. None of these was used for a value.

conditions.human_role: The contributor built the pipeline and the method, set the goals, chose the records and approved each publication. Language models ran the transcription passes, the fits, the decode, the readings and the checks inside that pipeline. No person checked the transcription against the images.

solution.what: Machine transcription of the 35 cipher pages of the 22 records from the DECODE images: a draft, a source check and a reconciliation for each page. 539 rows. Not verified by a person.

A key found from the ciphertext alone on 13 records (R74 to R78 and earlier transcriptions of 8 of these 22), with an Italian letter model and 100 starts (francia-346-leaves/README.md in the contributor's repository); fixed at 01:27 (UTC-3). 69 of its 80 pair codes show a letter. It has no three-digit codes (key-and-key-free-read/key-free-key.tsv).

Key-free check of the code counts of each record against the earlier letters, with control twins, before the published key was opened: 12 records fit, 6 differ, 4 too small to judge (key-and-key-free-read/READ-digit.md).
The key-free key applied to the 22 records with no new fit; the read fixed at 17:00 (UTC-3). It shows a letter for 0.911 of 12,896 pair tokens (key-and-key-free-read/READ-digit.md).

The frozen read graded against the published key: 98.8% of its shown true letters are right (6,930 of 7,017); all 87 wrong letters are code 07; 62.0% of its graded shown tokens are letter codes (7,017 of 11,324) (check.md).

The published key with the ledger's 28 three-digit values and pairs 88 and 33 applied to all 35 pages; the cut by a search with an Italian letter model. 10,919 code tokens, 92.3% with a value (10,081); 803 three-digit tokens with no value (README.md).

The decode aligned with the decipherment leaves of R5626, R5637 and R5646: 58.0%, 71.1% and 78.7% of the shorter text align with equal letters; the leaves of other records give 31.7% to 48.9% (check.md, section 7).

DECODE's public record pages, this ledger's catalogue and notes, and one study of Ceva (README.md). The DECODE pages of the 22 records give status N/A, cipher type Unknown and Inline Plaintext No; the word "Decryption" appears on each, but the documents need a login and were not opened. The ledger files no decipherment of these 22 records. Leman (1920) used clear minutes of this series; not checked.

Ten pages that read badly (R5642 f. 246r, R5643 ff. 249r-v, R5656 f. 337r, R5657 ff. 342r-v, R5658 ff. 344r-v and 345r, R5659 f. 351r) were transcribed again by machine on 12 and 13 November. The contributor's repository decodes them (francia-346-full/rereads.md): R5643 f. 249r reads in part; the others read in short stretches. This folder keeps the first transcription.

A declared correction of digits that the transcription may misread (8 read as 6, on the pages where 8 is rare and 6 is common) failed its own check on a page that reads; no page uses it (README.md, Limits; r5656.md).

A second pass graded each ledger value of a three-digit code against these letters: 14 certain, 7 probable and 25 conjecture (6 adopted values that the letters put in doubt, and 19 values that the ledger read off decipherments of 1632 but did not adopt); 129 stays open. Each ledger value was hidden in turn: aligned decipherments of the time gave none, a word-level score found 0 of 21, two readers found 5 and 1 of 21; so no new value. The pages show 515 three-digit tokens with a value and 639 open; 10,245 of 10,919 code tokens (93.8%) show a value (README.md).

parts.label: Key-free read, frozen before the published key was opened
parts.basis: Key from the ciphertext alone on 13 records (8 of them here), fixed 12 Nov 2026 01:27 UTC-3; read of the 22 records fixed 17:00; 98.8% of shown true letters right (6,930 of 7,017), but 62.0% of graded shown tokens are letter codes. The text does not build sentences.

parts.label: Decode with the published key and the ledger's values
parts.basis: First pass: 92.3% of 10,919 code tokens had a value (10,081). Second pass, graded: 93.8% (10,245) show a value; 639 three-digit tokens stay open. Each record page holds a partial reading and translation, but most sentences hold holes. By the read bar the documents are marked "decoded, not read", so the extent is none until a reader reviews them.

outcome.method_basis: The published key of Lasry, Megyesi and Kopal (2020), with three-digit values and two pair values from targets/ceva1632, graded in a second pass, applied to a machine transcription of the 22 records.

texts.label: R5626, Rome, 8 January 1633
texts.summary: Rome answers letters of 30 November and 3 December, and asks that "Monsieur di Botru" stop in a place (code 951). It wants the crowns brought to a perfect correspondence, and it names the death of a person whose name reads only as "S…co". Rome writes separately to Bichi about Venice and Ferrara, and it blames the conduct of a party (code 330).
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5635, Rome, 12 March [1633]
texts.summary: Rome acknowledges letters, one of them of the 21st of the previous month, and a talk with a Father called "Sua Paternità". The letter names an embassy and a declaration on the "[817]sione" of the plenipotentiaries. It says that through "della Carboniera" no effect is to be hoped for now.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5636, Rome, 2 April 1633
texts.summary: Rome answers letters of the first of the previous month and of 26 February, on a good [?peace] and a priory of San Ma[…]ino. It reports a rumour: a party (code 831), for a reward, wants a fortress on this side of the [Rhine?] that the [Swedes?] hold. It gives the answer of "S.E." on the plenipotentiaries and on the fortresses of Lorraine.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5637, Rome, [April] 1633
texts.summary: The letter speaks of an "ambasciaria" and of men at the court who work for the Church. The nuncio spoke well about the priory and about offers of pensions. Rome regrets that Benavides lacks something (codes 997, 119), and it refers to what a party (code 831) did with Botru.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5640, Rome, [April 1633?]
texts.summary: Rome wants a "ministerio" from both sides, so that the start of a negotiation is not cut off. Talks settle matters, but some things irritate minds and lead to a rupture; the point of [130] will be the most difficult. On the universal [?peace] Rome sees endless difficulties: if two [170] were settled, the others would be easy.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5642, Rome, 21 May 1633
texts.summary: The published key does not read f. 246r as Italian. The source marks each row of that page as a tentative reading, and the page has the mark of the 8-to-6 misreading. The four rows of f. 246v read in part, and they end "non concludere".
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5643, Rome, 28 May 1633
texts.summary: The source reads no sign in the 18 cipher rows of f. 249r. On f. 249v, 12 of 14 rows end in an unread run. So this record gives no reading.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5645, Rome, 2 July [1633]
texts.summary: The cipher stands in short pieces between clear lines. It names the reasons why the nuncio did not attend the solemnity of a "creatione". It also names a writing handed to Benavides, Rome's answer to it, and a public consistory.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5646, Rome, 9 July 1633
texts.summary: Rome hears from several sides that a woman (code 175) is ill and in danger. It wishes that she be reconciled with a "f…uolo" (perhaps a son) and return. Rome has read the writing given to Benavides and foresees that nothing will come of it.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5647, Rome, 23 July 1633
texts.summary: The cipher stands in five short pieces between clear lines. The pieces read only in part. They give no connected sense.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5648, Rome, 30 July 1633
texts.summary: Rome praises the nuncio's opening with [581] on [?peace] and union, and wants no one to irritate minds with aid and incitement. It warns against breaking the thread of the talks, and it names a break into war with [113]. On f. 279v, Rome regrets that the nuncio did not see a writing at once, and it regrets the illness of [175].
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5649, Rome, 30 July 1633
texts.summary: The cipher stands between clear lines. It deals with a restitution and with exchanges (permute) of church property. The letter says that the bull "de non infeudandis" also covers exchanges, and it names [?censures].
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5650, Rome, 20 August 1633
texts.summary: Rome judges the talk between [581] and Benavides useful: it prepares S.E. not to reject at once the answer to the writing. The nuncio must work for an answer that keeps the talks going. Rome fears that the [831] want to finish everything at once, and it sees the affairs of Germany as full of difficulty.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5651, Rome, 31 August 1633
texts.summary: Benavides has already given a written answer, which does not seem to satisfy. Rome says that proposals and answers, carried back and forth, settle matters, and that the nuncio must keep the talks going. On f. 297v, Rome discusses aid to a people (code 104) under old alliances, and it wants the business brought sooner to its end.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5652, Rome, [September 1633?]
texts.summary: Rome comments on the nuncio's talk with a person (code 797) and with Benavides. It says that two fortresses left with a party (code 831) would become almost impossible to restore. To take them back by force is full of difficulty and danger. f. 303v reads in part: it names talks in Vienna and Benavides.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5653, Rome, [after 30 August 1633]
texts.summary: Rome has [?seen] a writing or message of Benavides about [130], and the opposite view of [330]. It returns to the same point: to press from one side and the other with the reasons given before. Rome fears that the invasion of Lorraine will cause greater trouble between the crowns.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5654, [place and date not known]
texts.summary: Rome has heard with displeasure of the events in Lorraine. It has the words "per fermare questa rovina" (to stop this ruin), and it names openings to Benavides and the zeal and shrewdness of a person. It says that France will willingly embrace a thing, and that someone finds it useful to close his eyes.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5655, Rome, [12 November 1633?]
texts.summary: Letters from Germany (codes 930 957) report on "Monsieur della Carboniera" and on a move of arms. A neutrality is said to be violated, which someone has with the Swedes and with France; the Imperial court is displeased. Rome sees the [?hope] of a [?peace] between the crowns move away each day, and it speaks of the handling of "this holy work".
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5656, Rome, [date not known]
texts.summary: The published key reads this page only in fragments. The page has the mark of the 8-to-6 misreading: a high share of 6 and a low share of 8. An earlier exploratory variant read some 6s as 8; it is not a reading, and this page does not show it.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5657, Rome, [date not known]
texts.summary: The published key reads these pages only in fragments. The source marks each row of f. 342r as a tentative reading. That page also has the mark of the 8-to-6 misreading. f. 342v holds long unread runs.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5658, Rome, [date not known]
texts.summary: The source reads no sign in the cipher rows of f. 344r and f. 344v. The five rows of f. 345r read in part. They speak of someone's will, which will [?always] be the same, and of S.E.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

texts.label: R5659, Rome, [date not known]
texts.summary: The source reads only the first of the 22 cipher rows of f. 351r. That row reads only in fragments.
texts.note: The record page also holds a partial reading in Italian and an English translation.

outcome.notes: Contributed by prabal-rje as a pull request. The status, the class and the reading review are for the maintainer. documents[].length.tokens are the code tokens of the decode (README.md, table of records), not measured with docs/_check_profile.py. The scripts of the read, the grade and the decode are not in this folder. The digit rows are not in this pull request; TRANSCRIPTION.md says why. The 28 three-digit values of the first pass and pairs 88 and 33 come from targets/ceva1632 (cipher.py and the re-read of 22-23 Oct 2026), and 19 conjectures from its R75 and R84 readings; key-and-key-free-read/key.tsv marks each. outcome.verification leaves out "statistical test", because docs/_validate.py was not run; the key-free check of code counts and the bits per letter are in solution and README.md. first_break is false: the key of this cipher was published in 2020 (Lasry, Megyesi and Kopal, with readings of other letters of the dossier), and decipherments of the time exist for some of these records. The contributor's repository also holds pages for R5627 to R5634, R5638, R5639, R5641, R5644, R5660 to R5666, R5669 to R5671 and R74 to R78; they are not in this pull request.
